summary: The applied-state receipt is now carried by a source-grounded behavior instead of only by the measurement. Reading the conflict scan in appendEntries (raft.go 1522-1600, material append_new) shows reconciliation is decided by term alone: for each incoming entry at or below the follower's last index the follower reads its own entry at that index and deletes the suffix only when the terms differ, never comparing type or data, and a term-matching incoming entry is neither truncated nor appended. So a stored LogConfiguration entry and an incoming LogCommand at the same index both survive when their terms agree - exactly what receipt 8c866b71bf0e470e900a15e895b2bed9 records (LogConfiguration vs LogCommand at index 118, both sides applied through 121, a later client entry applied by every instance, and conflict_index 0 in the flag-disabled control). Effects: one knowledge created; validated (valid true, execution_requested false). I also note that the controller declined a bounded-completed stop request, so the audit stays open and the next executions worth running remain the fault and storage boundary cases: a disk-backed commit-tracking store, crash/restart timing, and the same partition observed through a snapshot transfer or a post-healing election.
